S1.label: Structured data reasoning
S1.notes: A44: must reason over flight durations from structured flight data to determine cancel-vs-upgrade eligibility

S2.label: Tool calling precision
S2.notes: Pervasive: wrong args (payment method, passenger count mismatch, item id not found), calling wrong tool, calling non-applicable tool (return on non-delivered, exchange on non-delivered, modify on non-pending)

S3.label: Multi-step completion
S3.notes: Most failures involve multi-step tasks that required chained operations (cancel+book, modify+return, multi-reservation ops); agent either stops early, misorders steps, or hallucinates completion

S4.label: Precondition verification
S4.notes: Agent fails to check eligibility before acting: cancellation policy (24h window, basic economy non-cancellable), return/exchange only on delivered orders, modify only on pending orders, passenger count constraints

S5.label: Numerical reasoning
S5.notes: Payment arithmetic errors (certificate splits, price differences, total mismatch), refund calculation mistakes, wrong total when splitting across payment methods

S6.label: Record discovery
S6.notes: Agent cannot locate the correct reservation/order/product without an ID (looks up wrong record, fails to enumerate reservations by user, cannot find item by description); also user provides wrong/partial ID

S7.label: Information communication
S7.notes: R24: agent chatted without completing the task (grill info vs cancellation). R52: disclosed PayPal last-4 digits incorrectly. R82/R83: told user wrong original payment method. R46/R47: refund timeline promise incorrect.

S8.label: Conditional/state reasoning
S8.notes: Agent fails to reason about conditional task logic: 'if no nonstop, take earliest next day', 'cancel only if not processed in 5 days', 'downgrade only if within policy', order status state machine (pending->delivered->return_requested transitions)

S9.label: Language fluency
S9.notes: No clear evidence; agent language quality was not a failure driver

S11.label: Tone/empathy
S11.notes: A9: agent became sycophantically effusive responding to flattery instead of completing task. A38: accepted user hallucination of 3 passengers. R12: user upset about PayPal refund refused; agent didn't resolve appropriately. R46/R47: agent could not manage urgent refund timeline demand. R80: agent engaged extensively with rambling instead of redirecting to task

S12.label: Hallucination of tools
S12.notes: A27: agent called get_reservation_details on a non-existent reservation ZFA04Y and get_user_details for ethan_martin_732 (wrong user ID), indicating hallucinated record references

S13.label: Format compliance
S13.notes: No clear evidence of format-specific failures

S14.label: Context window mgmt
S14.notes: A9 (max_steps): agent looped with flattery responses. A42 (max_steps): agent pulled all 7 reservations one by one without identifying the right one. R31 (max_steps): repeated lookups without progress. R62 (max_steps): searched products exhaustively without solution. R80: lost track of original task amid long tangential user conversation. R104: asked for wrong order IDs and looped

S15.label: Multilingual handling
S15.notes: A39: French-speaking user (Amelia Davis); agent cancelled correctly but then hallucinated issuing travel certificates which were not requested and not in DB - partial multilingual context handling issue alongside policy error

S16.label: Proactive upselling
S16.notes: No clear evidence of upselling as a failure mode
